title: Hosted SDK & Streaming: Architecture Deep-Dive — Scheduling
text:
Hosted SDK & Streaming: Architecture Deep-Dive — Scheduling

["From: Elena Morales <elena@atlashealth.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Atlas Health Engineering <eng@atlashealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: architecture deep-dive — SDK, streaming, function calls

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the hosted API overview last month. Our eng team at Atlas is diving into integration planning and they asked for a technical architecture session focused on your SDKs, streaming model responses, and tool / function-calling patterns.

High-level asks:
- Walkthrough of the SDK auth flow and retry/backoff behavior
- Streaming best practices for low-latency feeds (we'll have sub-second needs on some routes)
- How function/tool calling looks in production (webhook patterns, idempotency)
- Recommendations for KV cache / prefix caching for chat sessions

Would you and an engineer be available for a 60–90 minute deep-dive in the next 2 weeks? Our preferred window is the week of Nov 8, mornings PT. We can invite our infra lead and two frontend engineers.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Engineering
Atlas Health

--
Elena Morales
Atlas Health — elena@atlashealth.ai
", "From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: architecture deep-dive — SDK, streaming, function calls

Elena — thanks for the clear asks and timeline. Happy to run this; I'll lead the session and bring Marissa (solutions + SDK) and Olga (runtime/streaming). 60–90 minutes is perfect.

Proposed slots (PT mornings as requested):
- Tue Nov 9, 09:00–10:30 PT
- Wed Nov 10, 09:30–11:00 PT
- Fri Nov 12, 08:30–10:00 PT

Draft agenda (attached): RDW-Atlas-deepdive-agenda-v1.pdf — we plan: 1) quick context & goals, 2) SDK auth & retry, 3) streaming demo + latency tuning, 4) function/tool calling patterns, 5) caching/retries & rollout strategy, 6) Q/A and next steps.

Items we want from your side before the call: a short list of representative routes (expected RPS, typical seq lengths) and any compliance constraints for webhooks. Sharing a small sample event schema helps — I included sample-event-schema.json as an example of the payload shape we commonly see.

If the slots above don't work, tell us two that do and we'll follow up with a calendar invite + Zoom.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference

--
RDW internal: Please note Marissa will demo SDK streaming examples; Olga will cover runtime-level kernel/quantization tradeoffs.
", "From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Morales <elena@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: architecture deep-dive — SDK, streaming, function calls

Elena — I'll prepare two short demos:
1) SDK streaming integration (Node + Python examples) showing chunked responses and reconnection semantics
2) Function-calling pattern with webhook handshake and idempotency token sample

One ask: do you want us to show the difference between continuous KV caching vs per-session prefix caching with real numbers (latency/expense)? We can include a small benchmark slide if useful.

Also, if your infra lead is available for a 10-minute pre-call at the top to share exact RPS and sequence length distributions, that will help us tailor the examples.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
", "From: Elena Morales <elena@atlashealth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Atlas Health Engineering <eng@atlashealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: architecture deep-dive — SDK, streaming, function calls

Hi all — thanks for the agenda, looks great. We can do Tue Nov 9, 09:00–10:30 PT. I'll invite: Raj (infra lead), Mei (frontend), and Carlos (platform).

Raj can give you RPS and sequence distributions in a short pre-call note; I asked him to drop a quick write-up to the thread. Also: can you confirm if the SDKs support per-token streaming ACKs and how you recommend handling partial failures from downstream webhooks?

Elena
", "From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: architecture deep-dive — SDK, streaming, function calls

Perfect — slot confirmed and calendar invite sent: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=rdw-atlas-deepdive
Zoom link: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210?pwd=demo

Short answers to Raj's forthcoming note and Elena's question so you have context before the call:
- SDK per-token streaming ACKs: SDKs surface chunked events and provide a checkpoint callback you can use to persist offsets; we demo the Node callback and the Python iterator. For very low-latency streaming we recommend the iterative callback pattern (less allocation, lower GC).
- Partial webhook failures: recommend idempotency token + background retry queue (we'll show an example with exponential backoff + poison-queue handling). For synchronous routes where we need immediate success we suggest a hybrid: optimistic streaming to client + background webhook confirmation with a final commit message when webhook succeeds.

Attachments: RDW-Atlas-deepdive-agenda-v1.pdf, sample-event-schema.json

See you on the call — I'll include a 10-minute pre-call slot at 08:50 PT for quick infra handoff.

Best,
Karthik
", '']
